chapter: The China offer, wedding and Shanghai
title: The international settlement, English MCs and cheap tailored uniforms
summary: He recalls the MCs Ursula Preston and her partner, the many uniforms they bought, and the cheap hand tailoring.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: They all lived there, yes. International settlement. French, the Americans, the Russians, the English. And we had a beautiful Master of Ceremonies and Mistress of Ceremonies. I don't remember his name. Her name was Ursula Preston.

Yes. Both of them were from England. And they were ballroom dancers. And they announced our band every night and they were so immaculate and we were dressed in all, we bought so many different uniforms. We had eight or ten different uniforms.
We had white tails, black tails and grey tails. White suits. (LAUGHTER).

Yes, you see those tailors made everything by hand and so cheap. You couldn't believe. You got a suit for such a cheap amouht. So we really got stocked up on clothes. Because it would cost us too much money to buy in the States. All of them tailor made to everybody. And all these acts would come over from America and we would play for their acts. And it was just a wonderful two years.
Not the whole two years because we had some trouble there.
